The Glenside polka

There are 24 other names for this tune.

Also known as Andy Boyle’s, Battery #1, Battery Single #1, Battery Singles #1, The Battery, The Derryveeney, John Doonan’s #2, Kerry #1, Kerry #2, Kevin’s, The Listowel #2, The Listowel No. 2, The Listowel, The Mall, McElroy’s Fancy, Pat Horgan’s #2, Pat Organ’s #2, Single From The Battery #1, Singles From The Battery #1, Taoḃ An Ġleann, Tom Billy Murphy’s, Tom McGowan’s, Tony Lowe’s, West Limerick.

Re: The Glenside

I really like this one. I love how each part reminds me of a different tune: the first is reminiscent of an E dorian version of “The Ballydesmond Polka No. 1” ( https://thesession.org/tunes/298 ), and the second part is basically a polka version of the second part of “O’Keeffe’s Slide” ( https://thesession.org/tunes/53 ). Great tune!

↳ Posted by Daniel Parker on September 8th, 2017.

The Glenside, X:10

Newfoundland variant, played as a “single”.

From the “Singles from the Battery” set, alternatively known as the “Battery Singles” set. “The Battery” is a neighbourhood within St. John’s, so presumably musicians there popularized it on the island. It appears on Graham Wells‘ album in Ador/Amix, on Kelly Russell’s & The Planks’ album, and on one of The Irish Descendants’ albums in Edor.
